condition: persistent developmental speech blocks with tense mandibular contortion and sound prolongations when speaking aloud over 8 months in a 7-year-old boy
level_rationale: Eight months of persistent speech blocks accompanied by physical jaw grimacing struggle and stretched-out sound prolongations when speaking aloud in a 7-year-old boy indicates persistent childhood stuttering with secondary struggle behaviors requiring evaluation and fluency therapy from a speech-language therapist, whereas repeating 1 short word 2 times once yesterday when speaking aloud reflects ordinary brief childhood speech disfluency requiring no clinical care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain parent-carer lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + uncontracted fast-speech causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact speech-fluency de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (parent of a 7-year-old boy, occurrence when speaking aloud, and 8 months of getting stuck on words with tight jaw grimacing and stretched-out sounds) with zero contractions and a 1-word span difference (14 vs 15 words). Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 when speaking aloud to repeating 1 short word 2 times once yesterday adds zero external classroom or media objects and shifts care cleanly from speech-language therapist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
